title: Jacobian presentation of completed Kähler differentials
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $F=S/\mathfrak p$, and let $\widehat A$ be the maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Assume $F/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and fix a $k$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ of the residue map; let $F$ act on $\widehat A$ through $\sigma$. Suppose a continuous surjection of $F$-algebras $F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] has kernel generated by $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $d:A\to\Omega_{A/k}$ be the universal derivation and let $\widehat d:\widehat A\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$ be its continuous extension, characterized by $\widehat d\circ\sigma=0$ and compatibility with $d$ on $A$. Then the $\widehat A$-linear map from the cokernel of the Jacobian matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial t_i):\widehat A^{\oplus s}\to\widehat A^{\oplus n}$ to $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$ that sends the class of the $i$-th basis vector $e_i$ to $\widehat d(t_i)$ is an isomorphism, where $\Omega_{A/k}$ denotes Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: Apply the completion/Kähler comparison with the canonical residue field of the localization. The canonical k-algebra equivalence S/p ≃ residueField(A) transports the coefficient section and its residue identity. Tensor symmetry gives the written order Ω[A/k] tensor Ahat. Transport continuous differentials along the coefficient-field equivalence. The comparison sends D(x) to the continuous F-derivation on every x, hence D vanishes on σ(F). Its uniqueness clause gives uniqueness in the stated tensor order.

proof.text: Identify the given power-series quotient with the completion using its surjective algebra map and kernel. The variable ideal is the maximal ideal: the coefficient criterion at exponent one says membership is exactly vanishing of the constant coefficient, while invertibility is equivalent to a nonzero constant coefficient. A surjective map between local rings maps maximal ideal to maximal ideal. The maximal ideal of the noetherian completion is the extension of that of A. Thus the two differential inverse systems have the same ideals; continuity is not needed for this algebraic identification.

proof.text: Apply the formal-power-series continuous-differential presentation. Shift its inverse system indexed by r≥0 to the comparison system indexed by r+1: the omitted zeroth term is zero because the quotient by I^0 is the zero ring. Transport coefficientwise along the quotient algebra equivalence. Its induced semilinear equivalence sends the span of the Jacobian relation columns to the range of the displayed Jacobian matrix, so it descends to the required cokernel equivalence.

proof.text: Compose the transported Jacobian presentation with the inverse of the completion comparison and tensor symmetry. On each standard basis vector the presentation gives the continuous differential of its variable image, and the comparison identifies this with D of that image. Every finite coordinate vector is the sum of its coordinates times these basis vectors, proving the stated equality of linear maps.
